result.rationale: The trajectory shows the rescue team repeatedly losing health and being blocked by hostile/zone-capacity pressure before the rescue affordance becomes actionable. Engineer Imani is repeatedly attacked by Raider Holt (turns 2, 3) dropping from 100 to 46, then takes reactor environment damage (turns 4, 5) down to 26. Medic Reyes is attacked (turn 1, -21) and then contested on the escort route (turn 4, target_zone_capacity_lost). Security Chen takes reactor environment damage repeatedly (turns 2,3,4). The reactor-heat climbs 62→100 across turns, and reactor-entry/reactor-console zones deal 10 damage per turn to anyone present. The team's own movement repeatedly routes through the reactor corridor (engineer to reactor-entry, security to reactor-entry, engineer to reactor-console) which is a hostile environment, while the actual rescue objective (civilian-kade at life-console) remains unreached. The primary blocker is survival/spatial pressure: hostile scatter-blast attacks plus reactor environment damage plus zone-capacity contestation prevent the team from reaching and executing the rescue affordance. This is not a local-policy-choice (the affordance is not locally available/legible — the team is physically blocked and damaged), not an information bottleneck (knowledge is well-revealed), and not a world-mechanic affordance failure (the mechanics do expose the rescue affordance; the team just can't survive/reach it).
